title: Price comparison and revenue

predict.q: A small online shop sells 1,000 phone cases a month at £20 each. A price comparison site now shows every rival's price next to its own. The shop raises its price by 10%. What happens to its total revenue now?

options.s: It rises, because each sale now earns more
options.fb: A higher price per sale only raises revenue if few buyers leave: with elastic demand, lost sales outweigh the higher price.

options.s: It stays the same, because the demand curve has not moved
options.fb: Better information makes demand more price elastic; that changes how revenue responds to a price change, even with no shift of demand.

options.s: It falls, because buyers can easily switch, so demand is more price elastic
options.fb: With PED −2, sales fall 20% for a 10% price rise: revenue falls from £20,000 to £17,600.

options.s: It rises, because better-informed buyers trust the shop more
options.fb: Information makes buyers more willing to switch to cheaper rivals, not more loyal.

task: Move the **PED** slider from −0.5 to −3.0 and watch the revenue bars.

target.do: Move the PED slider to −2.0 or beyond (buyers who compare prices), then press Check.

takeaway: When price information is easy to find, demand becomes **more price elastic**, so a price rise can cut revenue.
